collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VIII: OUR OWN STORIES, SKILLS AND FUTURE (LCH-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume IV concepts (301-400): telling our own stories, who owns a song or a design, research the village asks for, caregivers and builders, seeds that came home, makers and stargazers, terrible singing, newcomers who stay, and an island that belongs to its people.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: An elder wants to teach dishes nobody makes anymore: cook them all for a feast, or teach one at a time.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) remembers dishes nobody makes anymore: seaweed cakes, smoked eel in leaves, a pudding made of roots that takes three days. (friend), a young cook, wants to learn them all. What should they do?

choices.label: Cook Them All for a Feast

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: They spend a week cooking. The feast is extraordinary and very strange. The eel is a triumph. The root pudding is a disaster. The village eats everything anyway, and asks for the eel again.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) teaches (friend) one dish a moon. By the end of the year, (friend) can make all of them, and has improved the root pudding, which (subject) refuses to admit.
